title: 2027 SARC/ACL R&D Internship Program – Multiple Engineering Teams
location: 3900 N Capital of Texas Hwy, Austin, TX, USA; 3655 N 1st St, San Jose, CA, USA
description: Position Summary Samsung, a world leader in advanced semiconductor technology, is founded on a simple philosophy: the endless pursuit of excellence will create a better world for all. At Samsung Austin Research and Development Center (SARC) and Advanced Computing Lab (ACL), we are building a center of excellence for Intellectual Property (IP) that is applied to high-performance computing devices consumed by millions of people around the world. Come build with us! Role and Responsibilities Through conversations with your recruiter and interviewers, we will learn about your technical background, experience, and interests, and work with you to identify the team where you can make the greatest impact and grow the most. Final team placement is based on that alignment and business needs. How We Hire One application, many possibilities. When you apply to our internship program, you are considered for all of our engineering teams at once, with team fit determined throughout the recruitment process. Tip: On your resume, highlight the projects, coursework, and tools most relevant to the areas that interest you. This helps us match you with the right team faster. Our Teams SARC/ACL is a full-cycle R&D center for GPU, System IP, SoC Architecture, and AI/ML acceleration. Our teams cover every stage of development, from architecture, modeling, and RTL design to verification, physical design, emulation, silicon validation, and software, powered by a dedicated engineering infrastructure. Skills and Qualifications Actively enrolled in an accredited U.S. college or university pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field. Available for a 12-week internship. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills. Effective written and verbal communication skills. Ability to collaborate and work effectively in a team environment. Demonstrated curiosity, initiative, attention to detail, and willingness to learn. Technical Skills Relevant coursework, projects, research, or experience in one or more of the following areas: Programming: C/C++, Python, Perl, Bash, Tcl, data structures, algorithms, and Linux. Graphics, GPU & AI: 3D graphics, Vulkan, OpenGL, DirectX, Metal, ray tracing, GPU computing, machine learning, and AI acceleration. Computer Architecture: CPU/GPU architecture, memory systems, cache coherency, SoC design, performance and power modeling. Hardware Design & Verification: Verilog, SystemVerilog, VHDL, RTL design, UVM/OVM, simulation, and digital verification. Physical Design: VLSI, logic synthesis, circuit design, floor planning, timing analysis, physical verification, and PPA optimization. Emulation & Silicon Validation: Hardware emulation, power modeling, silicon validation, hardware bring-up, and debugging. Software Development: GPU drivers, compilers, kernel/user-mode software, performance profiling, and automation. Infrastructure & IT: Linux, operating systems, HPC, networking, system administration, automation, and information security. Research: Computer architecture, graphics, VR/AR, machine learning, AI, and semiconductor technologies. Total Rewards At Samsung SARC/ACL, base pay is one part of our total compensation package and is determined within a range. This is a paid, hourly internship. Your actual hourly pay will depend on variables that may include work location, academic standing, relevant skills, qualifications, and experience. The base pay range for this internship is: Austin, TX: $38.40–$63.60 San Jose, CA: $48.00–$78.00 Samsung Interns have access to benefits including: medical, dental, and vision coverage, housing and transportation stipend, free onsite lunch, access to fitness center, wellness activities, organized social events, professional development courses and resources, dedicated mentorship with an experienced engineer, and many more. Trade Secrets By submitting an application, you agree not to disclose to Samsung or induce or encourage Samsung to use any confidential or proprietary information (including trade secrets) belonging to a current or former employer or other entity. U.S. Export Control This role may require access to information subject to U.S. export control laws. Applicants must be authorized to access such information or eligible for government authorization. #SARC #ACL * Please visit Samsung membership to see Privacy Policy, which defaults according to your location. You can change Country/Language at the bottom of the page. If you are European Economic Resident, please click here . * Samsung Electronics America, Inc. and its subsidiaries are committed to employing a diverse workforce, and provide Equal Employment Opportunity for all individuals regardless of race, color, religion, gender, age, national origin, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, status as a protected veteran, genetic information, status as a qualified individual with a disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

title: Research Intern - MSR Software-Hardware Co-design
description: Overview Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. We are a team of experienced research scientists in Microsoft Research. Our mission is to co-design novel and intelligent software systems and hardware-aware techniques to improve the efficiency, reliability, scalability, and trustworthiness of next-generation artificial intelligence (AI) systems. We build working systems, engage with academia, publish scientific papers, publish software for the research community, and deploy cutting-edge technologies. Are you excited by problems such as: Using AI agents to automate hardware experimentation, system management, and performance analysis. Reverse engineering the performance and security characteristics of modern graphics processing unit (GPU) servers and their memory systems. Understanding and overcoming performance bottlenecks in high-bandwidth GPU interconnects, such as NVLink and NVLink-C2C. Improving the efficiency of large language models (LLMs) serving by optimizing data movement and communication across central processing units (CPUs), GPUs, and memory systems. If you are, then we want to work with you! Our team has deployed research to a multitude of Microsoft businesses, including Azure AI, Azure Hardware, Azure Networking, and Windows. We have also published our research at the top systems and security academic conferences including ASPLOS, ISCA, USENIX Security, IEEE S&P, SOSP, ACM SIGCOMM, USENIX NSDI. As part of a small, tight-knit team, your work will be central to our focus and attention throughout the summer and beyond. Find out more about the team at: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/group/software-hardware-co-design-sharc/ . We practice open communication and respectful dialogue. We support multiple social and career building opportunities in our internship program. We seek Research Intern candidates with demostrated technical skills and backgrounds in computer systems, computer architecture, and/or AI. We are particularly interested in candidates who have experience in one or more of the following areas: GPU architecture and memory systems, hardware performance characterization, AI agents and automation, high-performance interconnects, and large-scale LLM serving. Candidates should have experience building and evaluating systems, proficient programming skills, and familiarity with state-of-the-art research in their area of expertise. We value candidates who are curious about how hardware systems work, enjoy designing experiments to uncover their behavior, and can translate their findings into practical software and systems improvements. Candidates should be comfortable working in a collaborative research environment and driving projects from initial ideas through implementation and evaluation. Responsibilities Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. Responsibilities may include: Using AI agents to automate hardware experimentation, system management, and performance analysis. Reverse engineering the performance and security characteristics of modern GPU servers and their memory systems. Understanding and overcoming performance bottlenecks in high-bandwidth GPU interconnects, such as NVLink and NVLink-C2C. Improving the efficiency of LLM serving by optimizing data movement and communication across CPUs, GPUs, and memory systems. Qualifications Required Qualifications Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering or a relevant field. Other Requirements Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit a minimum of two reference letters for this position as well as a cover letter and any relevant work or research samples. After you submit your application, a request for letters may be sent to your list of references on your behalf. Note that reference letters cannot be requested until after you have submitted your application, and furthermore, that they might not be automatically requested for all candidates. You may wish to alert your letter writers in advance, so they will be ready to submit your letter. Preferred Qualifications Experience building and evaluating research prototypes or engineering systems. Proficient programming skills and hands-on experience with systems software. Experience in at least one of the following areas: GPU architecture, memory systems, or hardware performance analysis. AI agents, tool-use frameworks, or automated experimentation. High-performance interconnects, Direct Memory Access (DMA), or CPU-GPU and GPU-GPU communication. LLM inference, distributed systems, or AI workload optimization. Experience with experimental methodology, performance profiling, and analyzing complex hardware-software interactions. Familiarity with relevant state-of-the-art research, demonstrated through research projects, publications, or prior industry experience. The base pay range for this internship is USD $6,810 - $13,480 per month. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $8,920 - $14,610 per month. Certain roles may be eligible for benefits and other compensation. Find additional benefits and pay information here: https://careers.microsoft.com/us/en/us-intern-pay Microsoft accepts applications and processes offers for these roles on an ongoing basis throughout the academic calendar (September - April). This position will be open for a minimum of 5 days, with applications accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled. Microsoft is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, citizenship, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, immigration status, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran or military status, race, ethnicity, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable local laws, regulations and ordinances. title: Silicon Photonic Design Intern
description:
About Marvell Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities. At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead. Your Team, Your Impact Your team develops silicon photonics-based optical engines and components at the heart of next-generation AI and Data Center infrastructure, directly shaping how AI systems connect and scale. Join a group of curious, highly motivated engineers embedded in a culture that is flexible, open, highly international and diverse, and genuinely people-centered. Zurich consistently ranks among the world's top cities for quality of living for expatriates and is Europe's leading tech hub, a city that seamlessly blends multicultural innovation with stunning natural surroundings. As an intern, you will work on real projects with mentoring from experienced engineers. You will see how photonic devices go from concept to design, layout, and tape-out. What You Can Expect Depending on your interests and the team's needs, you will: Support the simulation and design of passive and active photonic integrated components and circuits. Help translate device specifications into mask layouts, and learn the layout verification (DRC) and tape-out process. Contribute to scripts and tools for simulation and mask layout. Analyze measurement data and compare it with simulations to understand and improve device performance. Document your work and present your results to the team. What We're Looking For What We're Looking For: Currently enrolled in a Master's or in the final year of a PhD program in Electrical Engineering, Photonics, Physics, or a related field, with an expected graduation date after the end of the internship. Solid foundation in photonics, optics, electromagnetics, or semiconductor physics. Interest in silicon photonics, optical communications, and photonic device design. Some hands-on exposure to simulation or design through coursework, a thesis, or projects (for example, FDTD, FEM, or mode solvers). Programming or scripting skills (Python preferred). Nice to have (any of the following): Experience with photonic electromagnetic simulation (Lumerical preferred). Experience with RF or EM simulation (HFSS preferred). Experience with code-based photonic IC layout. You Also Bring: Curiosity and initiative, with the ability to work independently on a well-scoped project. Openness to feedback and eagerness to pick up new tools and topics quickly. Clear written and verbal communication, including presenting your results to the team. A collaborative attitude and willingness to learn from and work with colleagues across teams. 

 Additional Compensation and Benefit Elements With competitive compensation and great benefits, you will enjoy our workstyle within an environment of shared collaboration, transparency, and inclusivity. We’re dedicated to giving our people the tools and resources they need to succeed in doing work that matters, and to grow and develop with us. For additional information on what it’s like to work at Marvell, visit our Careers page. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status. Interview Integrity To support fair and authentic hiring practices, candidates are not permitted to use AI tools (such as transcription apps, real-time answer generators like ChatGPT or Copilot, or automated note-taking bots) during interviews. These tools must not be used to record, assist with, or enhance responses in any way. Our interviews are designed to evaluate your individual experience, thought process, and communication skills in real time. Use of AI tools without prior instruction from the interviewer will result in disqualification from the hiring process. This position may require access to technology and/or software subject to U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). As such, applicants must be eligible to access export-controlled information as defined under applicable law. Marvell may be required to obtain export licensing approval from the U.S. Department of Commerce and/or the U.S. Department of State. Except for U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, or protected individuals as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), all applicants may be subject to an export license review process prior to employment. #LI-SC1

title: Product Engineering Failure Analysis Intern

As a Product/Test Engineering Intern, you'll support the development and implementation of strategies that achieve profitability targets on assigned TI product lines through new product development, cost reduction, capacity expansion and yield enhancement projects. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Testing and troubleshooting issues Developing production and characterization test specifications Creating and managing product documentation Providing product development support, which involves interfacing with design, test engineering, quality engineering, and other groups Designing, debugging, and correlating test hardware and software Designing interface and measurement circuits to make tester capabilities compatible with product definitions You could work in one of the following roles based on degree: Software Engineer Mechanical Design Engineer Product Engineer Test Engineer You'll have direct involvement in the entire lifecycle of the products in your assigned product portfolio, including product definition, qualification, manufacturing, cost optimization, and quality. In addition, you will have the chance to resolve customer quality and application issues, and facilitate cross-functional teams in problem solving activities. Texas Instruments will not sponsor job applicants for visas or work authorization for this position. Minimum Requirements: Pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical & Computer Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or related field Cumulative 3.0/4.0 GPA, or higher Preferred Qualifications: Strong verbal and written communication skills Demonstrated strong analytical and problem solving skills Ability to work in teams and collaborate effectively with people in different functions Ability to take the initiative and drive for results Strong time management skills that enable on-time project delivery Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced and rapidly changing environment Demonstrated ability to build strong, influential relationships Coursework providing knowledge and background in semiconductor processing, process control methodology and/or device failure analysis. Proficiency with bench level test equipment (i.e., DC power supplies, oscilloscopes, multi-meters). Experience with LabView, Spoffire, MatLab, JAVA, C++, and/or other programming skills Why TI? The future starts here. As a TIer, you'll play a critical role in defining the next era of semiconductor technology and help create the innovations that shape the world around us. Surround yourself with a team of innovators who value your unique perspective and will challenge you to bring your best self to work every day. We believe that fostering a culture of collaboration fuels both personal growth and technological breakthroughs. Explore our company culture . At TI, your success goes beyond your work. Take advantage of comprehensive benefits designed to support your total well-being at work and in life, from competitive compensation to extensive health coverage and wellness programs. Learn more about our benefits offerings . About Texas Instruments Texas Instruments Incorporated (Nasdaq: TXN) is a global semiconductor company that designs, manufactures and sells analog and embedded processing chips for markets such as industrial, automotive, data center, personal electronics and communications equipment. At our core, we have a passion to create a better world by making electronics more affordable through semiconductors. This passion is alive today as each generation of innovation builds upon the last to make our technology more reliable, more affordable and lower power, making it possible for semiconductors to go into electronics everywhere. Learn more at TI.com . Texas Instruments is an equal opportunity employer and supports a diverse, inclusive work environment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, disability, genetic information, national origin, gender, gender identity and expression, age, sexual orientation, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. If you are interested in this position, please apply to this requisition.

title: Mechatronic Apprentice I
description: Operations is at the heart of Amazon’s business. We are known for our speed, accuracy, and exceptional service. Our buildings deliver tens of thousands of products to hundreds of countries worldwide, every day. Reliability Maintenance & Engineering (RME) are the business partners that work tirelessly behind the scenes to make it all happen. We drive continuous improvement, and maintain all of the Robotics and Material Handling Equipment (MHE) to ensure our customers are met with the Amazon smile. Come join us on our journey! About the Role: As a Mechatronics & Robotics Apprentice (MRA), you will learn to combine electronic, mechanical, computer and automation engineering skills at the workplace. During on-the-job learning (OJL) you will work with complex high-performance manufacturing systems and will learn to analyze, troubleshoot, and repair systems to maintain process efficiency. The focus of your role will be to learn the skills and abilities to ensure safety regulations and policies are adhered to, assist in the installation, maintenance, and repair of the automated packaging and distribution equipment, ensure preventative maintenance is conducted on time to a high standard, and provide high levels of equipment availability through continuous improvement. You will be paired with journey workers to carry out their work at various facilities, including high automation and robotics facilities in connection with service operations. You will be expected to complete work based on technical documents and instructions and carry out your work in compliance with the relevant provisions and safety regulations. You should be an effective communicator, work well in a team, and be self-motivated. You must have the ability to work collaboratively and coordinate your activities with upstream and downstream operations partners. In addition to developing your skills, you will be mentored by senior technicians to grow in your role. Key job responsibilities - You will perform preventive and predictive maintenance on conveyance equipment and robotic work cells following established job plans. - You will conduct basic troubleshooting and corrective maintenance on robotics systems. - You will troubleshoot electrical and mechanical problems across material handling equipment components, using schematics, technical documentation, and hands-on diagnostic techniques to isolate and resolve root causes. - You will maintain, inspect, and replace electromechanical components, such as motors, photo eyes, relays, proximity sensors, solenoids, motor starters, tachs, etc. under the guidance of senior technicians. - You will support the maintenance team with inspections, work order documentation, and any other assigned tasks as directed by site leadership. Physical requirements: You must be able to move up to 49lbs, stand and walk during shifts lasting up to 12 hours, climb ladders and gangways safely, and without limitation, as well as perform regular bending, lifting, stretching, and reaching both below the waist and above the head Program Requirements: • Flexible to relocate after completion of the program • Able to enroll in and attend a 9-week training at one of four designated training providers • Meet the minimum qualifying score on a Mechanical Aptitude Test Please note that while we strive to accommodate employees' preferences for shift assignments, due to operational requirements and scheduling constraints, we cannot guarantee a specific shift assignment. - High School Diploma - 1+ years of PC software experience including Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook experience - Experience troubleshooting and repairing operational items - Knowledge of mathematics - Experience measurement reading and interpretation - vocational/technical training or an associate degree or above, or 1+ years of Amazon RME (Reliability Maintenance Engineering) experience, or 2+ years of military service (E-2+) experience - 4+ years of military experience - Experience conducting predictive and preventative maintenance procedures - Experience troubleshooting and diagnosing material handling equipment (MHE) - Experience implementing safety standards - Experience reading blueprints and electrical schematics Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner. The starting pay for this position is listed below, including the base pay rate plus the highest available shift differential which applies depending on the shift you select. As a total compensation company, additional earnings may include shift differentials and overtime pay. Final pay will be based on factors including shift selection and location. Starting Day 1 of employment, Amazon offers EAP, Mental Health Support, Medical Advice Line, 401(k) matching. Learn more about our benefits at https://hiring.amazon.com/why-amazon/benefits . USA, AZ, Phoenix - 27.00 - 29.00 USD hourly

title: Hardware Test Engineering, Intern (Summer 2027)
description: Lightmatter is leading the revolution in AI data center infrastructure, enabling the next giant leaps in human progress. The company invented the world’s first 3D-stacked photonics engine, Passage™, capable of connecting thousands to millions of processors at the speed of light in extreme-scale data centers for the most advanced AI and HPC workloads. Lightmatter raised $400 million in its Series D round, reaching a valuation of $4.4 billion. We will continue to accelerate the development of data center photonics and grow every department at Lightmatter! If you're passionate about tackling complex challenges, making an impact, and being an expert in your craft, join our team of brilliant scientists, engineers, and accomplished industry leaders. Lightmatter is (re)inventing the future of computing with light! About this job Are you ready to do meaningful internship work on technology that is changing how AI systems are built? The System Level Test team owns the final at-speed test of our silicon photonics products. These are cutting-edge high-speed optical interconnects built to move data between the processors that power AI datacenters, where copper is running out of reach and light is taking over. We build the test methods, the automation, and the data behind the pass vs fail decision. This summer's project is a hands-on optical characterization and correlation study aimed at improving how our products are tested in production. You will work on real optical hardware in the lab, build the measurement automation, generate the data, and write the recommendation that decides whether the approach moves forward. The result will directly influence how our next products are tested. Responsibilities: Characterize a set of silicon photonics units on bench optical instrumentation, measuring output power, modulation amplitude, extinction ratio, and wavelength. Build automation to run measurements, control the lab setup, and log results in a consistent, reusable data format. Correlate unit measurements against a calibrated laboratory reference and quantify per-unit offsets and population spread. Measure unit stability across time, temperature, and repeated re-insertion, and analyze repeatability and drift. Deliver a feasibility and gap assessment with a clear recommendation, including the calibration and maintenance scheme needed for production deployment. Requirements: Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's program in Electrical Engineering, Physics, Optical Engineering, or a related field. Coursework or project experience in at least one of: integrated circuit design, device or circuit characterization, or electrical or optical testing. Hands-on experience with standard lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, multimeters, power supplies, or optical power meters, from coursework, research, or a prior internship. Programming experience in Python or a similar language, including reading and plotting measurement data. Preferred Qualifications Research, lab, or prior internship experience in photonics or semiconductors. Experience automating lab instruments (PyVISA, SCPI, or similar). Familiarity with basic statistics: mean, standard deviation, repeatability, and gauge or measurement uncertainty. Publications, projects, or open-source contributions related to the role. description: Come join Analog Devices (ADI) – a place where Innovation meets Impact. For more than 55 years, Analog Devices has been inventing new breakthrough technologies that transform lives. At ADI you will work alongside the brightest minds to collaborate on solving complex problems that matter from autonomous vehicles, drones and factories to augmented reality and remote healthcare. ADI fosters a culture that focuses on employees through beneficial programs, aligned goals, continuous learning opportunities, and practices that create a more sustainable future. About Analog Devices Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI ) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. With revenue of more than $11 billion in FY25, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible. Learn more at www.analog.com and on LinkedIn and X . Design Evaluation Engineer, Power Management ICs Analog Devices is seeking an Entry-Level Design Evaluation Engineer to join our Power Management IC engineering team in San Jose, California starting Summer 2027. This hands-on laboratory role is designed for an engineer with a Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering or a closely related discipline who wants to build expertise in post-silicon evaluation, validation, characterization, and test automation. You will evaluate power-management integrated circuits such as step-down and step-up converters, low-dropout regulators, and related mixed-signal power products. Working with experienced engineers, you will plan and perform laboratory measurements, automate test equipment, analyze results, investigate unexpected behavior, and communicate clear technical conclusions. This role is well suited to someone who enjoys working with real hardware, learning how integrated circuits behave across operating conditions, and using experiments and data to solve engineering problems. Essential Responsibilities Perform hands-on laboratory evaluation and characterization of power-management ICs, including buck converters, boost converters, LDO regulators, and related mixed-signal functions. Support first-silicon and evaluation-board bring-up under the guidance of experienced engineers. Execute validation plans across input voltage, output voltage, load, switching frequency, operating mode, temperature, startup, shutdown, and fault conditions. Measure parameters such as output accuracy, line and load regulation, efficiency, power loss, quiescent current, ripple, noise, transient response, switching behavior, current limit, and thermal performance. Capture and analyze oscilloscope waveforms for startup, shutdown, mode transitions, load transients, switching nodes, protection events, and other dynamic behavior. Develop Python/C# scripts to control laboratory instruments, automate parameter sweeps, collect data, create plots, and improve measurement repeatability. Review test data for consistency, identify anomalies, and apply structured troubleshooting methods to isolate measurement, board, system, or silicon-related causes. Compare bench measurements with design expectations, simulations, datasheet limits, and automated-test results as appropriate. Assist with evaluation-board schematics, component selection, board bring-up, rework, fixture development, and review of power-layout and measurement considerations. Collaborate with Design Engineering, Applications Engineering, Product Engineering, Test Engineering, and Manufacturing teams to resolve technical issues and support product introduction. Continue developing expertise in power electronics, analog measurement, test automation, data analysis, and post-silicon validation. Minimum Qualifications Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a closely related engineering discipline, completed or expected before the employment start date. Graduate-level foundation in analog circuits, electronics, and circuit analysis. Academic understanding of power electronics or power-management circuits, including at least one of the following: linear regulators, buck converters, boost converters, feedback systems, or switched-mode power supplies. Hands-on laboratory experience gained through university courses, research, thesis work, internships, teaching laboratories, student teams, or engineering projects. Familiarity with oscilloscopes, digital multimeters, bench power supplies, and electronic loads. Basic programming ability in Python or another technical programming language. Ability to organize data, create plots, compare results, and communicate observations clearly. Demonstrated curiosity, attention to detail, willingness to learn, and ability to collaborate respectfully with others. Clear written and verbal communication skills. No prior semiconductor-industry employment is required. Preferred Qualifications Coursework, research, or project experience in power electronics, analog integrated circuits, feedback and control, semiconductor devices, or mixed-signal systems. Exposure to automated instrument control using Python, PyVISA, LabVIEW, C#, MATLAB, or similar technologies. Experience measuring power-supply efficiency, ripple, noise, startup, load transients, or loop behavior. Familiarity with schematic capture, PCB layout, SPICE simulation, or evaluation-board development. Exposure to oscilloscopes with differential or current probes, SMUs, spectrum analyzers, network analyzers, thermal equipment, or EMI measurement. Familiarity with digital control interfaces such as SPI, I²C, or PMBus. Experience documenting technical work through a thesis, laboratory report, publication, design review, or project presentation. Why Join Our Team? Join a team where graduate-level circuit knowledge becomes hands-on engineering experience. You will work directly with advanced power-management ICs, modern laboratory equipment, evaluation hardware, automation software, and real post-silicon data. You will learn from engineers across Design, Applications, Product Engineering, Test Engineering, and Manufacturing while contributing to products used in industrial, communications, instrumentation, automotive, and other demanding applications. The role offers a path to build specialized expertise in power electronics, precision measurement, silicon debug, automated validation, and data-driven product decisions.
